newsitem.title: USA: Eastman cites plastic prices, propane for Q4.
newsitem.headline: Eastman cites plastic prices, propane for Q4.

text.p: Eastman Chemical Co Tuesday reported weaker fourth-quarter earnings, citing substantially lower selling prices for Eastapak Pet packaging plastic and higher costs for propane.

For the quarter, the company reported net earnings of $60 million, or $0.77 per share, compared with $1.50 per share a year ago. Sales fell nine percent to $1.11 billion from the year-ago's $1.22 billion.

Earnest Deavenport, Eastman's chairman and chief executive officer, said the company expects significant volume growth for its Eastapak Pet because of increasing demand and additional capacity, although prices will likely remain under pressure due to significant industry capacity increases. The company also plans incremental gains in capacity for fibers and various chemicals products.

Deavenport also said Eastman plans to improve its cost structure in 1997. "As part of our previously announced goal to remove $500 million from our cost structure by the end of this decade, we are targeting $100 million in labor and materials productivity improvements in 1997."
